articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Racing Santander vs Valencia
articles.standfirst: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Racing y al Valencia en El Sardinero, correspondiente a la jornada 8 de LaLiga
articles.summary: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Racing y al Valencia en El Sardinero, correspondiente a la jornada 8 de LaLiga
articles.body: El Racing de Santander recibe al Valencia este domingo (21:00 h) en El Sardinero, en el regreso de LaLiga tras el parón de selecciones. El campeón de Segunda llega con 7 puntos y la sensación de que su fortaleza está en casa. Sus dos victorias (3-2 al Elche y 2-1 al Alavés) y su empate (2-2 con el Villarreal) han llegado en Santander, mientras que fuera ha perdido los cuatro partidos, entre ellos goleadas de 7-2 en el Camp Nou y 5-0 en Vigo. El Valencia, por su parte, es penúltimo con 4 puntos, una victoria, un empate y cinco derrotas, y estrena entrenador. Javier Aguirre, que sustituye a Carlos Corberán, destituido el 13 de septiembre. Favorito para el partido entre Racing y Valencia El mercado ve un partido muy abierto. Bet365 sitúa la victoria del Racing a 2.3, el empate a 3.6 y el triunfo del Valencia a 3. Las casas de apuestas dan una ligera ventaja al conjunto cántabro por su rendimiento como local y por la crisis del Valencia, aunque el historial y la plantilla che mantienen el choque lejos de estar decidido. Los valencianistas llegan tras perder 2-3 ante la Real Sociedad y suman su única victoria a domicilio en Vitoria (0-1). Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan es una de las opciones más atractivas para las apuestas deportivas, sobre todo por la fragilidad del Racing. El equipo de José Alberto López ha encajado en los siete partidos que ha jugado en Liga (21 goles en contra, tres por encuentro) y ha marcado en cinco de ellos. En El Sardinero, además, ha visto puerta y la ha visto recibir en los tres partidos. El Valencia es más irregular arriba, pues solo ha marcado cuatro goles en siete jornadas y ha dejado la portería rival a cero en cuatro ocasiones, pero logró marcar en dos de sus tres salidas, incluido el 2-3 del último partido. Con un equipo nuevo y mejores sensaciones tras el cambio de técnico, la apuesta por el sí paga a 1.53, por 2.38 del caso contrario . Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles señala un partido de muchos tantos. Los partidos del Racing tienen una media de 4.6 goles por encuentro (11 a favor y 21 en contra) y han superado los 2.5 goles en seis de siete ocasiones, solo se quedó corto el 0-1 en Getafe. En los del Valencia, la media baja a 2.4 por choque, pero el equipo ha sido muy vulnerable atrás: 13 goles encajados, incluidos un 0-5 ante el Barcelona y un 1-3 en La Coruña. Si el Racing mantiene su ritmo ofensivo en casa y el Valencia sigue concediendo, el más de 2.5 goles paga a 1.67, frente a 2.2 del menos de 2.5. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante. La pasada temporada en Segunda División, el Racing fue uno de los equipos que más saques de esquina botó, con unos 240 en 42 partidos (una media de 5.7 por encuentro), y presentó un estilo muy ofensivo en el juego aéreo. Ante un Valencia en pleno proceso de reconstrucción y con tendencia a replegarse tras los resultados adversos, es probable que los locales acumulen llegadas por las bandas. Por ello, la apuesta es el más de 10.5 córners a 2, por 1.73 del caso contrario.

articles.title: Verstappen cierra el círculo: reina en la noche que da a Antonelli la 'bola de Mundial'
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés gana, por fin, en Singapur y los españoles pelean sin premio en forma de puntos
articles.summary: El neerlandés gana, por fin, en Singapur y los españoles pelean sin premio en forma de puntos
articles.body: Max Verstappen ha cerrado el círculo. Era un lunar extraño que su histórico palmarés no tuviese éxito alguno en las calles de Singapur, pero esa herida desapareció. El neerlandés arrasó en Singapur, se lleva los 33 puntos del fin de semana y ya es vencedor en todos los circuitos de la Fórmula 1 excepto Madring, estrenado hace un mes. El título es un imposible para el tetracampeón, pero junto a la mejora del Red Bull es el claro animador de un final de campaña en el que quiere ganar todo lo que esté a su alcance. El título, claro, sólo responde a Kimi Antonelli y las cuentas hacia una corona que es cada vez más real tras subir al podio. Después de estar alejado y sufriendo con los límites durante muchas vueltas, el italiano apareció en el tramo final con habilidad para desesperación de Norris y Hamilton. Su renta de puntos ya está en 102 y en Austin puede proclamarse como campeón del mundo tras el 9º de Russell con una remontada estéril. Por la victoria, el argumento fundamental de Verstappen se sostuvo entre la arrancada y una batalla estratégica bonita. Como ocurrió en el sprint, Max no tuvo el mejor tiempo de reacción y el 0,21 en la salida de Leclerc dibujó el primer ataque al pegarse al muro. Pero el neerlandés es de los que jamás abrirá una puerta y alargó la frenada para que sólo el de Ferrari pudiese pasar jugándose el tipo. Cosa que no ocurrió. La película pasó a ser del juego de paradas. Arrancó con un intento de Hamilton desde lejos (vuelta 19) con un blando que no pudo exprimir al encontrarse detrás de Leclerc, las quejas del británico en la radio y la puerta abierta tras un coche de seguridad virtual. Ferrari quiso mantener al heptacampeón en pista y metió a su compañero, que tenía mejor posición en pista. Sin alejar a Norris o Antonelli, bastante cerca siempre. Allí Hamilton perdió todas sus opciones. Porque el neumático del '44' se vino abajo (sexto en meta) y la batalla contra Norris y Antonelli se abrió. Allí, el alumno aventajado demostró que su título no sólo es por el cohete de Mercedes. Los dos británicos entraron en batalla, el de Ferrari terminó saliéndose fuera y el vigente campeón se quedó sin potencia. Era el camino despejado para que Kimi atacase y ponga el Mundial a tiro en los Estados Unidos. La acción del brillante italiano colocó el broche de un final bonito, acompañando en el cajón a un Verstappen que no tuvo rival. Arrasó de inicio a fin, amargó a los Ferrari y Leclerc, segundo en meta, se queda con el consuelo del cajón. La gloria y otro triunfo más van para el talento del neerlandés. Nadie es capaz de pararle. Carlos Sainz vivió la cara amarga de la moneda en Singapur. Su temporada trata de maximizar lo que aporta la mecánica del FW48, pero las limitaciones son totales. En el urbano nocturno se repitió, pues firmó una salida de escándalo en la que forzó un cuatro en paralelo para colocarse 10º. Pero acto seguido, la batería -y toda opción a resultado- se vino abajo en el Williams. En apenas dos vueltas perdió la plaza de puntos con los Haas y su carrera pasó a la supervivencia. Que trataba de mantener atrás a coches más rápidos, como Hadjar, y ver que le pasaban conforme el Williams caía de rendimiento. Ni una buena parada mejoró el resultado final, 14º. Uno de sus findes más difíciles porque las causas ajenas cortan cualquier oportunidad. Más atrás todavía terminó Fernando Alonso (16º). El que era la esperanza principal del final de campaña, sólo señaló los errores de base que son letales para esta F1. Y el motor está en el centro. "Es ridículo", llegó a decir tras una relanzada de coche de seguridad virtual al romperse el Audi de Bortoleto. En pista, un imposible. Sí dejó un adelantamiento por agresividad a Bottas en la 13, pero era consciente de que poco más podría rascar. Las que buscaron en Aston Martin tienen que ver con una degradación que sigue siendo su gran argumento. Sólo Russell retrasó más su parada que Alonso, y tras entrar en la 36 regresó a su lugar natural después de rondar el puesto 14 en varias vueltas. Finalizó el 16º en un fin de semana que estaba marcado en rojo. La historia de la temporada.

images.caption: Verstappen defiende su posición ante Leclerc. RED BULL RACING

articles.title: Singapore Grand Prix result: Max Verstappen wins from Charles Leclerc with Kimi Antonelli third
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen secures his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli.
articles.body:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second dominant victory within a week as he secured his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix.

Verstappen fought off an attack from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc off the start line to control the race from start to finish.

The win followed his and Red Bull's maiden victory of the year in Malaysia last weekend and sprint race success in Singapore on Saturday, confirming the team's re-emergence as a major force.

Leclerc took second as team-mate Lewis Hamilton finished sixth after a baffling strategy that was a consequence of the Briton choosing not to pit when asked.

Hamilton, trying to last out on a set of soft tyres for a mammoth 44 laps, lost out in the closing laps to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

Antonelli's third place combined with team-mate George Russell finishing only ninth after starting from 19th extends the Italian's championship lead to 102 points.

That means it is possible for Antonelli to clinch his first world title at the next race, the United States Grand Prix on 25 October.

To become champion in Austin, he would need to win the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower.

Verstappen's dominance reviving memories of his pomp during his title-winning era

A confusing day at Ferrari with regard to strategy

Verstappen knew he needed to get into the first corner first to try to win the race, given the difficulty of overtaking in Singapore, and he fought tooth and nail to make sure he did.

Leclerc got a better start than Verstappen off the line and challenged down the inside as they approached Turn One.

But Verstappen squeezed him tight towards the pit wall and with their entry to the first corner so compromised, Leclerc eventually backed off and the four-time champion could claim the corner.

Verstappen, Leclerc and Hamilton ran nose to tail for the first four laps before the seven-time champion began to drop back from about lap five.

Leclerc stuck within a second of Verstappen for a further five laps before the Red Bull began to edge away from him as well.

From then on, Verstappen continued to build his lead and never looked like being beaten as he motored away into the distance.

"I think the last few races have been really positive for us and it is just great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results," said Verstappen.

"It is a really good group of people - I really enjoy working with them and hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year."

In the interviews immediately after the race, Antonelli was told he can win the title in Austin and responded: "Can I? Really? Let's not worry about that, let's try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job."

Hamilton had started on the medium tyres while Verstappen and Leclerc chose the softs. Despite his theoretically more durable tyres, the Briton pitted on lap 18 to switch to the softs, while Leclerc waited until lap 24 to swap his softs for mediums.

Leclerc came out of the pits from his stop just ahead of Hamilton, who had stronger pace on his softer tyres.

Yet Ferrari chose not to order Leclerc to let Hamilton through to maximise his pace, a decision that was questioned by Hamilton from the car.

A virtual safety car was called on lap 39 and Leclerc and Antonelli, who had chased the Ferraris closely from the start from his fourth place on the grid, took the opportunity for a cheap pit stop - it takes 10 seconds less to stop under a safety car than under racing conditions.

Yet Hamilton, despite having older tyres, did not stop, a decision that promoted him to second behind Verstappen.

As Leclerc was catching Hamilton, the Briton was told he needed to stop again; he pushed back to suggest he try to go to the end, but was told they were six laps short to make it in terms of tyre life.

Leclerc soon caught Hamilton and passed him on lap 46 and set off after Verstappen, but could get no closer than 7.3 seconds to the Red Bull.

Hamilton never did stop, but as his tyres lost grip he fell back into the clutches of Norris and Antonelli.

A passing attempt by Norris on lap 54 with eight to go saw Hamilton run off track and take to the escape road at Turn One, but as he did, Antonelli grabbed the chance to pass the McLaren, and then Hamilton later on the same lap.

Norris followed him through, and now Hamilton fell back towards the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri, who passed him on the final lap after a resolute attempted defence from Hamilton.

It was Hamilton's call not to stop and he apologised for it on the slowing down lap.

Russell's fight back through the field took him up to seventh as he delayed his pit stop as long as possible.

But after dropping back to 10th behind Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Alpine's Pierre Gasly, he passed Gasly after trailing him for 10 laps or so, but could not make it past Hulkenberg, who was himself chasing Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar took the final point in 10th after starting from the back.

It's off to the Circuit of the Americas in Austin for the United States Grand Prix, from 23-25 October, where 20-year-old Antonelli has his first opportunity to become the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history.

articles.title: Raúl Fernández y su tensa reunión en Aprilia con Bezzecchi: "Dije: 'Si quieres jugar, jugamos'"
articles.standfirst: Hicieron las paces y todo se relajó tras subir ambos al podio
articles.summary: Hicieron las paces y todo se relajó tras subir ambos al podio
articles.body: "El domingo ha sido muy bueno, pero eso no empaña lo del sábado, que fue muy malo", decía Massimo Rivola, el CEO de Aprilia Racing, que no estaba feliz del todo pese al 'póker' de su marca en la carrera del Gran Premio de Indonesia de MotoGP. Por cierto que el directivo dio la razón a Raúl Fernández por el incidente en la salida del Sprint. "Bezzecchi debió irse más al interior", soltó en DAZN. En el 'warm up', al acabar, en el ensayo de salida, 'Bez' se colocó tras el madrileño y éste se giró recriminándoselo. Luego, la carrera larga suavizó todo. Marco ganó y Raúl fue segundo. En el parque cerrado hubo un amago de abrazo por parte del de Rímini y, después, en el podio y luego, ya se hablaron de forma más relajada. Claro que, antes de la carrera, hubo una reunión para aclarar todo. Fernández pudo aguantar al dolor y subió al cajón. “Esta mañana me he levantado pensando que no corría. No tengo palabras. La carrera es lo menos importante. Siento que he corrido con todo lo que tenía; creo que ha sido la carrera más dura de mi vida. He tenido que cambiar la forma de frenar esta mañana, de frenar con un dedo, a frenar con el corazón y así es como he corrido. El problema es que tengo el dedo roto (índice) y no puedo moverlo. Si no es por los ‘fisios’ no habría podido correr. Ellos me han hecho un ‘tapping’ (fijación) en el dedo, que, básicamente, se ha quedado apoyado en la moto. He empezado a frenar con el dedo corazón esta mañana y las referencias eran muy malas. Lo único que puedo decir de la carrera es que, al final, no estaba pudiendo frenar como tocaba, me estaba yendo siempre un poquito largo y me consumía la goma trasera. Es el único pero que puedo poner. A partir de ahí, dar las gracias a mi familia. Ayer fue un día muy bonito y a la vez muy difícil. Hoy ha sido todo lo contrario, así que es momento de disfrutarlo, pero, sobre todo, de recuperarme bien, porque viene otro circuito muy favorable para nosotros. Dar las gracias a toda esa gente que se ha levantado esta mañana a apoyarnos; ayer, todos los mensajes que recibí de ánimo y de apoyo”, decía en DAZN. El del Trackhouse estaba feliz por el esfuerzo. “No me enfado o no estoy frustrado por una consecuencia de carrera, creo que nos exponemos a esto. Como dije ayer, ni mucho menos me voy hoy cabreado a dormir porque me haya roto un dedo, porque creo que eso ha sido consecuencia de una caída y ya está, no hay errores. Me iba un poquito más frustrado por cómo se dio esa caída. Hoy, junto a Davide (Brivio), hemos afrontado nuestra carrera, nuestro fin de semana. Daba igual quién tuviéramos delante, el objetivo era intentar ponerse primero y gestionar. Es verdad que a falta de 13-14 vueltas, no podía más. Creía que estaba fallando muchísimo con la frenada, no era nada regular y he intentado sobrevivir. Segundo, más que inmejorable. Ni de lejos esta mañana pensaba que podía hacer podio”, indicó. El de San Martín de la Vega desvelaba parte de lo hablado en esa 'reconciliación'. “Esta mañana, quería jugar. Yo le he dicho: ‘Si quieres jugar, jugamos, pero creo que no merece la pena. Somos dos personas que nos quedamos en Aprilia la temporada que viene, creo que tenemos que dar la mejor imagen para la marca’. Después del ‘warm up’, hemos tenido una reunión con Massimo (Rivola), Fabiano (Sterlacchini) y Davide y yo les he sido muy claro. Le he dicho: ‘Yo no vengo aquí a jugar con nadie, si quiere que abramos la veda, la abrimos, pero creo que no es momento’. Entre todos se ha calmado el agua”, admitió. 'Bez' quitaba hierro a todo. "Yo nunca he estado tenso. Son cosas que pasan en la pista. Hablamos. Raúl pensaba una cosa; yo pensaba otra. Nos hemos disculpado con la fábrica por nuestros errores”, manifestó en DAZN.

images.caption: Raúl Fernández, Bezzecchi y Jorge Martín, en el podio. EFE

articles.title: Así queda el Mundial de F1 y con posible título a la vista
articles.standfirst: Antonelli se dispara a los 102 puntos sobre Russell y hace sus primeras cuentas
articles.summary: Antonelli se dispara a los 102 puntos sobre Russell y hace sus primeras cuentas
articles.body: Kimi Antonelli, con 20 años y en su segunda temporada en F1, se perfila como el próximo campeón del mundo de F1. Así queda la clasificación tras su podio en Singapur, donde salió sexto, pero fue remontando hasta el tercero final, mientras Russell fue noveno, tras salir 19º por sanción de cambio de motor. Un poco más abajo, Verstappen ha pasado este fin de semana a Norris y a Leclerc y se queda a 8 puntos de Hamilton. Podría incluso ser segundo al final del campeonato.

images.caption: Antonelli, agotado tras ser tercero en Singapur. F1.com

articles.title: Sainz: "No sé qué pasa con la FIA, que nos está tocando todo lo feo"
articles.standfirst: Termina 14º, con problemas de baterías en las cinco primeras vueltas, tras la no sanción a Hulkenberg del sábado.
articles.summary: Termina 14º, con problemas de baterías en las cinco primeras vueltas, tras la no sanción a Hulkenberg del sábado.
articles.body: Carlos Sainz vio sus dos calificaciones en Singapur condicionadas por dos errores de la FIA. El primero cuando se quedó (con otros coches) sin el modo adelantamiento el viernes. La segunda el sábado cuando un fallo en el cronometraje eximió a Hulkenberg de pagar por estorbarle en la Q2. Arrancando desde el 13º, se colocó 10º tras la salida, pero luego, un problema de baterías en su Williams le hizo perder posiciones con los Haas a los que había rebasado antes. "La verdad que hasta la vuelta 1 estaba yendo todo increíble, después de la buena qualy de ayer. Hoy sabía que todo pasaba por hacer una buena salida y tomar riesgos, saliendo con los blandos", valoraba. "Y por el lado limpio quería arriesgar para ver si me colaba en los puntos y ver si aguantaba luego. Y la verdad que la salida ha salido muy bien. Pero a partir de ahí, desgraciadamente, problemas con la batería las 5 primeras vueltas.... Y luego una vez se ha estabilizado el problema, no teníamos ritmo para puntuar hoy. Así que tarde o temprano nos hubiesen adelantado y desgraciadamente hemos visto que el coche hoy no tenía ritmo", resumía sobre lo sucedido en Singapur, donde retuvo detrás a Lindblad muchísimas vueltas con un coche bastante más veloz. Sobre los problemas con la FIA por el error humano del viernes y la no sanción de Hulk el sábado, no tiene mucha explicación para el madrileño. "No sé qué pasa este año con la FIA, que a Williams y a mí en particular nos está tocando todo lo feo. Hacer la Q1 de la sprint sin potencia, que ayer claramente me impidiesen una vuelta y no le penalicen... Cuando a mí me pusieron 3 puestos sin pensárselo... Y los 5 puestos de la bandera amarilla de Baku, cuando sí que levanté. Está claro que no sé qué pasa este año, que nos han mirado mal, pero es lo que hay". "No nos están quitando puntos, tampoco porque tenemos tantos problemas con el coche que tampoco nos está yendo la vida en ello. Pero esperemos que el año que viene no sea así", deseaba. Carlos está contento con su pilotaje en general todo el fin de semana. "Los momentos en los que he podido marcar la diferencia la he marcado, pero luego desgraciadamente, cuando todos entramos en ritmo de carrera, sale a reducir un poco lo que tiene cada uno y ahí nos quedamos", analizaba

articles.title: Singapore GP: Max Verstappen wins event for first time in F1 career ahead of Charles Leclerc as Lewis Hamilton apologises for strategy
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore Grand Prix with a lights-to-flag victory; Charles Leclerc was second and Kimi Antonelli third; Lewis Hamilton apologised for a messy race strategically that saw him finish down in sixth
articles.body:
Verstappen led every lap on his way to a second consecutive win despite being unable to communicate with the team due to a radio problem, but it did not affect him as he held off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who eventually finished seven seconds behind in second.

Kimi Antonelli took advantage of an elbows-out battle late on between Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, with the seven-time world champion on old tyres in the latter stages, to take third and extend his lead over George Russell to 102 points in the Drivers' Championship.

It means Antonelli can become world champion at the next race in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 , should he outscore Russell by 23 points and Hamilton by 14 points.

Russell recovered to ninth in Sunday's race after starting 19th due to grid penalties for a new power unit, as overtaking proved very difficult at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

Reigning world champion Norris was fourth ahead of McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri, who also overtook an ailing Hamilton late on.

Hamilton apologised to the team for his strategy, suggesting he made some of the decisive calls that led him to fall down the order on old tyres.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson had another strong result in seventh with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg in eighth, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar went from the pit lane to the points in 10th.

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, Alpine's Franco Colapinto, Aston Martin's Lance Stroll and Williams' Alex Albon all retired with reliability issues but no full Safety Cars were required.

Verstappen dominates as Hamilton strategy goes wrong

Coming into the race, pole-sitter Verstappen was concerned about the start as Red Bull have been among the worst starters on the grid throughout 2026.

Leclerc in second had a better initial getaway to almost draw fully alongside Verstappen into Turn 1, but the Dutchman smartly pinched the Ferrari driver and had a better angle to swoop around the outside and, crucially, keep first place.

It looked like Ferrari had more pace early on as Leclerc consistently stayed within one second of Verstappen during the opening 15 laps. However, Verstappen was managing his tyres and began to stretch his lead as the first stint went on, ending up nine seconds ahead by the time Leclerc pitted on lap 25.

The advantage Verstappen built meant he could pit on lap 33 and still emerge in the lead. A Virtual Safety Car for Stroll coming to a halt saw Leclerc pit for fresh softs on lap 39 but he was unable to reel in his 17-second deficit to Verstappen, who won on his 250th grand prix start.

"The last few races have been really positive for us. It's just great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to deliver even more results," said Verstappen.

"It's a really good group of people, I really enjoy working with them, and hopefully we can have a bit more fun to the end of the year."

The main story of the Singapore Grand Prix saw a bold strategy by Hamilton go completely wrong, which the British driver held his hand up for post-race.

Starting on mediums, which seemed to be a worse race tyre compared to the softs, Hamilton, in third, was the first of the front-runners to pit on lap 19 so he could get onto the softs as early as possible.

He set some impressive lap times on fresh rubber but was stuck behind Leclerc after the Monegasque driver made his pit stop onto the mediums.

Hamilton felt he was getting held up and when the Virtual Safety Car came out for Stroll's stoppage, Ferrari called him to pit and double stack behind Leclerc, but Hamilton decided to stay out.

"Sorry boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one," said Hamilton on the radio after the chequered flag.

This left him vulnerable for the remainder of the race on ageing soft tyres as Leclerc quickly caught and overtook him, but that was the least of his problems.

Norris and Antonelli were also catching at a rate of knots and Hamilton thought he could hold on, given the difficulty of overtaking. He got his elbows out against Norris, cutting the first chicane in their battle for third which enabled Antonelli to take fourth from the McLaren driver, before he also passed Hamilton a lap later.

Eventually Norris got through and so did Piastri, who was forced to pit for a second time due to a slow puncture. Given Ferrari were hoping to challenge Verstappen for victory, Hamilton's sixth will be massively frustrating for the team.

Formula 1 next heads to The Americas for another triple header with the United States Grand Prix in Austin up first on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

articles.title: A Alonso le golpea el surrealismo: "¡Qué motor tan ridículo"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano vuelve a sufrir con un motor al que ni el nuevo turbo ayuda y sus esperanzas en Singapur desaparecen
articles.summary: El asturiano vuelve a sufrir con un motor al que ni el nuevo turbo ayuda y sus esperanzas en Singapur desaparecen
articles.body: Fernando Alonso cruzó la bandera a cuadros de Singapur mucho más lejos de lo que esperaba. Era el Gran Premio que favorecía al Aston Martin por su habilidad en curva lenta y degradación, pero la unidad de potencia Honda cambió el paso al AMR26. Rozó una buena remontada en el sprint y en carrera alcanzó al 16º tras alargar su parada y salir alejado por el cambio en el motor Honda previo. Ningún premio. Además, la carrera fue extraña. Porque vivió momentos con los que no contaba, como una reanudación tras coche de seguridad virtual en el que sufrió. "La energía... es ridículo este motor", soltó a su motor en la radio. Después lo precisó en el corralito ante la prensa internacional. "Hubo muchos despliegues de energía problemáticos al no desplegar en el momento y lugar equivocado, el coche no sabía dónde estaba y fue frustrante. Perdimos muchos puestos y terreno", explicó. "Podía pasar a Pérez... y me adelantó Hadjar", añadió. El triplete se salda con un octavo en Malasia y el bajón de siete días más tarde. "Siempre puedes pensar que obtendrás más del coche si vuelves a hacer la carrera. Y tuvimos problemas de subviraje que no pudimos resolver", analizó el asturiano. Con más dudas en el Aston pese a que la pista beneficiase. "En Sepang no tuvimos problemas y en Bakú tampoco en los primeros sectores. Parece un problema de esta pista y no tenemos respuestas", concretó. Con el expediente x del motor. Cortó cualquier opción que la apuesta por los neumáticos, el brutal adelantamiento en la 13 a Bottas o su agresividad podría generar. "El motor no rindió como debía. Debemos entenderlo porque vienen varias carreras difíciles como México, que tiene curvas lentas. Además de Las Vegas y otros urbanos. Hay que resolverlo, con la manejabilidad y el retraso del turbo, que nos cuestan mucho tiempo y lo descubrimos por las malos", argumentó. "En general, un fin de semana muy difícil", resumió. Con esa repetición, aunque por causas diferentes del motor de GP2 de los tiempos de McLaren, y un sufrimiento total. "Todas las vueltas eran difíciles... en cada recta perdíamos 200 o 300 metros", concluyó.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for costly decision to override strategy call during Singapore GP
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton dropped from third to sixth in the Singapore Grand Prix after choosing not to pit under a Virtual Safety Car; Hamilton was called into the pits by his Ferrari team but opted to stay out; the seven-time world champion required medical checks as he felt unwell after the race
articles.body:
Hamilton was running in third behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc on the 39th of 62 laps when a Virtual Safety Car appeared to give him the perfect opportunity to change tyres after he had been the first driver to stop earlier in the race.

Ferrari told Hamilton to follow Leclerc into the pits, but he ignored the call and stayed out, which resulted in him finishing the race sixth as he was overtaken by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in the closing stages.

After taking the chequered flag, Hamilton said on team radio: "Sorry boys. I let you down today with that strategy.

"My call, and I lost us valuable points.

"I'll try and make up for it in the next one."

The result saw third-placed Hamilton fall 111 points behind championship leader Antonelli, while his advantage over race winner Max Verstappen was reduced to just eight points.

Hamilton was excused from fulfilling his media duties after the race as he felt unwell after competing in the sweltering conditions, but he released a statement via the team.

"Today wasn't the result we were looking for and it was on me," Hamilton said. "At a track that's difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work. Unfortunately the Medium didn't perform as well as the soft.

"I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn't make the progress I needed. Under the VSC, the team called me in but I missed the entry. After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car today.

"A painful lesson today, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I'm sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them.

"I'll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race".

Vasseur: Call to Hamilton was crystal clear

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur confirmed after the race that Hamilton had ignored the pit wall's instructions.

"We called him, we called them both to pit," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1 .

"It would have been P2-P3 because we were P2-P3 on track, and he missed the pit entry, and honestly it's a bit of a shame because he's losing a podium also.

"It was crystal clear on the radio. But now let's be focused on Austin. The performance this weekend was ok. We have to be focused on the future."

Hamilton had been frustrated earlier in the race at being held up by Leclerc, as the pair's different starting tyres left them on different strategies.

Leclerc began on the soft tyre and Hamilton the medium, with the former turning out to be better performing. When Hamilton switched to the soft at the first round of pit stops, he found himself behind Leclerc, now on the medium tyre, with more pace.

Vasseur explained that Ferrari went into the race "blind" on which tyre would perform better because Saturday's Sprint had taken place in wet conditions on intermediate tyres, and the team hoped the split would boost their chances of challenging Verstappen, who cruised to victory from pole position.

"Today the soft was much better than the medium. That's why Lewis struggled at the beginning and a bit less at the end.

"I think we were all in the same situation starting the race a bit blind, and it's true that for us with the two cars second and third, it was a good opportunity to take different options to fight with Max."

Schiff: Hamilton has lost trust with Ferrari

Sky Sports F1's Naomi Schiff said Hamilton's decision to ignore the pit wall was not surprising due to a loss of trust between driver and team.

There have been multiple occasions this season where Hamilton has not been happy with his team's strategic choices, most recently at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

"I'm not that surprised though," Schiff said. "I think that they've sort of lost trust with each other on making the right decisions in certain circumstances.

"Do you blame Lewis today? Yes, maybe he made the wrong call. But do you blame the team last week? Yes, they made the wrong call then.

"So, I understand why Lewis is challenging them because he's not always confident that they're going to make the right decision.

"And maybe today he just really desperately wanted to get ahead of his team-mate and get that track position that on a track like this can sometimes make the difference.

"Let's not forget that before the VSC, they split the strategy, Lewis went in quite early on his mediums, had a fresh-ish set of softs when Leclerc came out in front of him, and Lewis didn't get to maximise that part of his stint because Charles was slowing him down as well.

"So, I do think there is a little bit of having to take control in some cases from Lewis' side because he doesn't really think he's going to get the best out of them."

Sky Sports F1's Jenson Button praised his former team-mate for offering an immediate apology.

"I really respect him for apologising at the end of the race," former world champion Button said. "Straight after the race is the best way to do it, and now they move on."

Button also rejected the suggestion that trust issues were a factor in Hamilton's decision.

"I disagree [that it was an issue of trust]," Button added. "I think he just wanted to make his call on the race, and he thought it was the right one.

"He didn't want to be sat behind his team-mate for the rest of the race, basically. He wanted to give it a go, and he knew his pace was there when he was on the soft tyre."

articles.title: Hamilton acaba destrozado físicamente y sin atender a la prensa tras perder el podio
articles.standfirst: El británico lanzó una estrategia poco eficiente y no pudo defenderse en las vueltas finales de carrera. Leclerc sí salvó su podio (P2)
articles.summary: El británico lanzó una estrategia poco eficiente y no pudo defenderse en las vueltas finales de carrera. Leclerc sí salvó su podio (P2)
articles.body: Una imagen al finalizar la carrera del Gran Premio de Singapur y con los pilotos en fila para dirigirse al pesaje obligatorio de la FIA resumió todo a la perfección. En ella, Lewis Hamilton tenía que agacharse mientras esperaba al turno. Poco después, se sumó que Ferrari explicó que no iba a pasar por el corralito de prensa tras encontrarse mal. Había luchado, había sufrido y se marchaba con un sexto sin sabor. Y Charles Leclerc... en el podio final. Ferrari tuvo una pequeña ventana de oportunidad para cambiar las cosas en Singapur, pero la estrategia naufragó al intentar atacar al intratable Max Verstappen. No funcionó el lejano undercut de Hamilton, tampoco pudo pasar a Leclerc pese a insistir por la radio y con el coche de seguridad virtual llegó el casino. El monegasco colocó un juego fresco y Hamilton se quedó con el mismo blando en pista. Era la tumba a cualquier opción porque ese neumático no iría muy lejos. Pero no existe un 'culpable'. Al cruzar la meta, Hamilton asumió toda la responsabilidad: "Lo siento, chicos. Les he defraudado con la estrategia. Fue mi decisión, nos costó puntos y espero compensarlo en la próxima. Gran trabajo en las paradas". En primera persona, el británico confirmaba su error. Cosa que en el equipo también dieron por válido. "Ha sido cristalina su radio. Les pedimos entrar a los dos, y éramos segundo y tercero en pista. Pero no entró y es una pena al perder su podio", reconoció Fred Vasseur, cuestionado jefe de los de Maranello. Que en Singapur no tiene culpa alguna. Leclerc peleó y Hamilton tuvo ambición sin premio. En pista, a Ferrari no le salió la cosa. Y fuera, Hamilton terminó destrozado, en una carrera físicamente muy exigente, con sólo una parada y sin ninguna neutralización. Tuvo que ser revisado por el equipo médico tras faltar a sus compromisos con la prensa y demostró la otra cara del infierno de Singapur. Pese a que la F1 ya no es la de siempre, el calor y la humedad hacen estragos. Además, su final de Mundial se complica para el tramo final. Max Verstappen ha sumado 58 de los últimos 58 puntos disponibles y se aproxima a poder superar a Hamilton en el podio final. Sólo les separan ocho unidades y George Russell apenas tiene 17 de renta con el holandés. El título, por supuesto, está en la mano de Kimi Antonelli.

articles.title: Singapore Grand Prix: Harry Benjamin's driver ratings as Max Verstappen wins again
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Singapore Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Max Verstappen took his second win in a row with victory from pole position at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The Dutchman also won the final sprint event of the campaign at Marina Bay and has moved up two places in the drivers' standings from sixth to fourth.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli finished third and has extended his title advantage over Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who was ninth, to 102 points.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Singapore.

Pretty much the definition of a perfect weekend. Pole and victory in both the sprint race and grand prix, and once George Russell crashed out of the sprint on Saturday there was barely a moment where Red Bull's Verstappen looked like losing control of either race.

Consistently Verstappen's closest challenger and took two podiums from the weekend. Third in the sprint followed by second in the grand prix was about as much as Ferrari could realistically have asked for.

Another hugely mature weekend from Mercedes' championship leader. Fourth in the sprint and fourth in qualifying before fighting his way on to the grand prix podium late on, despite dealing with brake concerns and flirting a little too often with track limits.

Sunday was solid enough, with fourth probably the maximum McLaren had on outright pace. But his collision with team-mate Oscar Piastri in the sprint cost both drivers heavily, and prevents this from being rated as a particularly strong weekend.

The victim rather than the instigator of McLaren's sprint collision and recovered with a decent Sunday performance. A slow puncture forced an extra stop but he still chased down and passed Lewis Hamilton for fifth, although seventh in qualifying left him with plenty of work to do.

His Saturday was excellent - a brilliant start helped turn sixth into second in the sprint before he qualified third for the main race. Ran in the podium places for much of Sunday too, but his decision to stay out on worn tyres backfired badly and eventually dropped him to sixth.

A really impressive weekend for Racing Bulls' Lawson. Fifth in the sprint, ninth on the grand prix grid and seventh on Sunday meant points in both races and another reminder of just how strong his recent form has become.

Another very useful weekend for Audi. Took points with seventh in the sprint, narrowly missed Q3 and then finished eighth in the grand prix, holding Russell behind late on in the process.

The pace deserved a much higher score. Fastest in practice, second in sprint qualifying and sensational off the line to take the sprint lead. However, throwing it into the wall at the end of lap one was a major mistake. Recovering from 19th on the grand prix grid to ninth was an excellent response from the Mercedes driver.

Almost everything that went wrong before Sunday was outside of his control. Mechanical trouble on his Red Bull ended his sprint and reliability problems meant he couldn't set a qualifying time, so recovering from the pit lane to score a point was an excellent drive.

Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win

Hamilton apologises to Ferrari as Antonelli moves to brink of title

Eighth in qualifying was one of the stronger midfield performances of Saturday. Just missed the points in both races and comfortably led Alpine's challenge across the weekend, even if there wasn't quite enough race pace to convert it.

A particularly good sprint where he produced a smart move on Gasly and came home sixth. He qualified P12 and the grand prix was less spectacular, but scoring three sprint points still made this a useful weekend for Haas' Bearman.

Finished 10th in the sprint and 13th in the grand prix without ever really looking like threatening Haas team-mate Bearman's points haul. A fairly anonymous weekend in which Briton Bearman had the upper hand.

Starting the sprint from the pit lane immediately made life difficult and there was little improvement afterwards. Qualified in 14th and finished there, making this another frustrating weekend for Williams.

There was obvious pace in qualifying, where he reached Q3, but the rest of the weekend was a lot messier for the Racing Bulls driver. Spinning to the back in the sprint and then slipping from 10th to 15th on Sunday meant the potential never really translated into a result.

Aston Martin had hoped Singapore would suit the car but it never materialised. Alonso was only 17th in qualifying and finished there on Sunday after an equally quiet sprint.

Another difficult weekend for Cadillac. His sprint ended almost immediately after contact with Lance Stroll, and 20th in qualifying left him with little chance of recovering on Sunday, eventually finishing 17th.

A messy sprint included the three-car incident with Gabriel Bortoleto and Valtteri Bottas before the Williams driver eventually retired. Qualifying 17th didn't offer much encouragement either, and another retirement late in the grand prix completed a poor weekend.

Caught up in the sprint collision involving Albon and Bortoleto, before qualifying 21st for the grand prix in his Cadillac. Reaching the finish on Sunday was about the only positive, three laps behind the winner.

His sprint was over on the opening lap after the collision with Perez, for which neither driver was penalised. Qualified 19th before a clutch problem ended his race midway through.

Not much chance to build any momentum across the weekend. Retired early from the sprint, hit the wall on his final qualifying lap and then suffered a suspected driveline or gearbox-related technical issue on his Alpine in the grand prix.

His sprint retirement came in the three-car accident with Albon and Bottas, so there wasn't much he could do about that. P15 in qualifying was less impressive, before another early retirement on Sunday brought a frustrating weekend to an end for the Audi man.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian finally gives Martin Brundle a Formula 1 interview after snubbing him at the Monaco Grand Prix
articles.summary: Kim Kardashian finally gave Martin Brundle the interview she denied him at Monaco, offering a playful apology on the Singapore Grand Prix grid.
articles.body: All is forgiven. The great Monaco Grand Prix snub of Martin Brundle by Kim Kardashian has finally been put to rest. All is right in the world of Formula 1, or so we can hope. Kim K gave Brundle the interview he was after back in June when he approached the new F1 WAG during his grid walk and was completely ignored by Lewis Hamilton's girlfriend. The two reconnected on Sunday at the Singapore Grand Prix. She turned her head to the side apologetically as he approached, then gave him a skillfully executed face-to-face sorry, not sorry. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Did I not know the rules? Did we get off on the wrong foot?" Kim replied to Brundle after he asked her how she was. The veteran broadcaster told her it was "absolutely fine," then went about getting the answers to questions he was after all those months ago. He asked her next, "What do you think of our crazy world of Formula 1?" If you aren’t already seated, I'd go find a seat. Otherwise, you could very well be blown away by Kim's answers to these questions. F1 STAR LEWIS HAMILTON REVEALS THAT HE SUFFERED A SERIOUS NECK INJURY IN A TESTING CRASH "I think it's amazing and fun and wild, and something I’ve never seen before," she said. "It’s amazing." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE What does she think about her man, Lewis, and his current driving form? Was he confident before climbing behind the wheel in Singapore? "He is [in great form]. I’m just praying for the best tonight," Kim said. As to whether he was confident beforehand, "Yes, very confident, and so am I. Just got to pray for the best." Props to Brundle for putting the snub aside and giving Kim Kardashian another chance. Imagine an alternate universe where he didn’t approach her again, and he didn’t get the answers to these questions. You're braver than I am if you're able to do that. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER I suppose we'll never get an answer or a pretend apology from Kim for stealing Kimi Antonelli's post-race towel, which also took place at Monaco. As for Sunday's race in Singapore, Max Verstappen won it. Kim Kardashian's confident man, Lewis Hamilton, finished in sixth place.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli relieved Max Verstappen is not in 2026 F1 title fight after Red Bull driver dominates Singapore GP
articles.summary: Max Verstappen made it back-to-back wins with a dominant victory at the Singapore Grand Prix; Kimi Antonelli can win the drivers' title next time out in Austin and is relieved Verstappen is not closer; watch the US Grand Prix from October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Verstappen scored maximum points across the Sprint weekend in Singapore to add to his victory earlier this month in Malaysia but, unlike last year, is too far back to make a championship charge.

In fact, Antonelli could wrap up the title at the next race in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 , if he outscores Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 23 points and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 14 points.

Antonelli had another damage limitation weekend in Singapore but still finished on the podium in third after a good strategy call by Mercedes to give him fresh soft tyres to overtake McLaren's Lando Norris and Hamilton late on in Sunday's race.

It was an unexpected result given the new upgrades, which Mercedes introduced in Malaysia, were not giving the major performance gain the team expected.

"It would be very scary!" Antonelli told Sky Sports F1 when asked if he is glad Verstappen is not in this year's championship battle.

"All in all I feel like we are doing a great job. At the end, you look at the season, and we have always been there.

"Obviously we have had a great car and now we are trying to understand this new package. I'm very proud of the team this weekend because we pushed through the difficulties and started to see life at the end of the tunnel. It's just a matter of time.

"Now we go to Austin, a normal weekend, where we can hopefully do a lot of changes and understand the package more."

Antonelli, 20, is set to break Sebastian Vettel's record of being the youngest F1 world champion and has six races to get over the line.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff is usually cautious with his expectations but even he admits Antonelli is almost certainly going to win the title.

"You look at the numbers and ask the probability of him winning, and it's probably almost 100 per cent. But it's motor racing, you can break down, you can have accidents, and then things could start to stress," he told Sky Sports F1 .

"So, I think we need to look at it race by race, make sure that we are continuing to score the points, and eventually hopefully it's going to come towards him."

Verstappen: Maybe Lambiase was happy radio was not working!

Red Bull's recent resurgence appears to have ended Mercedes' large dominance over the season, although Verstappen's win in Singapore was not straightforward as he was unable to talk to the team for the whole race.

Verstappen, who has won at every track on the calendar apart from Madrid, could hear his engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, but not the other way around.

"Maybe he was happy that it was not working! I couldn't really say anything. He did try at one point to ask me a few things in code, and I think he understood well what I meant or did not do," said Verstappen.

"But it's never nice. I've been having difficulty with my radio already the whole season, and this weekend has been particularly bad."

The biggest threat to Verstappen's win came at the start from Charles Leclerc as Red Bull have been poor off the line throughout 2026.

However, Verstappen got a good enough launch to move to the inside and pinch Leclerc, forcing the Ferrari driver to brake early and back out of the move.

"The start was critical, so that was just good enough. Something was not particularly right at the start, so I need to understand what went wrong there," he said.

"Before releasing the clutch, it didn't feel good. But it was just good enough. Then we had a few laps with some deployment issues, so that's where Charles almost got me actually into Turn 7.

"Once we had cleared the deployment problems, it was fine. The car was really good on the tyres. I could really manage them well.

"But to be honest, I think it was one of the first times that I've driven in clean air here in Singapore in the race, so I guess that's also nice.

"It's been just a fantastic weekend for us. I mean, we were flying on the soft, we were okay on the medium, and then of course with the VSC, I think it was right what Charles did with pitting and going back on a soft tyre. But, we just had it under control and of course, really happy to win here."

articles.title: Singapore Grand Prix: Lewis Hamilton apologises to Ferrari as Kimi Antonelli moves to brink of title
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton's incorrect strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix means Kimi Antonelli can win the world title at the next race in Austin.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team after overriding the pit wall and choosing his own strategy during the Singapore Grand Prix.

Ferrari were on course to finish second and third with Charles Leclerc and Hamilton, but instead the seven-time champion fell back to sixth in the closing laps as he fought a losing battle to hold off three cars while on fading tyres.

Hamilton apologised to the team over the radio on the slowing-down lap after the race, saying: "Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur said: "Clearly we asked them to pit. Charles pitted. Lewis didn't want to pit because he... I don't know why. And then he realised it was the wrong call. It's why he apologised to the team.

"Now it's not a drama for me that he made the wrong call. I'm making mistakes, he's making mistakes, we're all making mistakes sometimes. Now we have to look ahead and make mistakes positively."

Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win

Verstappen perfect and Antonelli hugely mature - driver ratings

Hamilton did not speak to the media after the race after saying he felt unwell and being given permission to miss the interview zone, known as the media pen.

In a statement released by Ferrari, he said: "Under the virtual safety car, the team called me in but I missed the entry. After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car.

"A painful lesson, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I'm sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them. I'll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race."

Ferrari called both cars in to the pits during a virtual safety car that was called mid-race. Stopping under the VSC saves about 10 seconds versus stopping under racing conditions.

Hamilton said in the statement that his decision was based on his improved pace on the soft-compound tyre after he had been forced to make an earlier pit stop than planned because the medium tyre on which he started the race was not performing.

"At a track (where it's) difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work," he said.

"Unfortunately the medium didn't perform as well as the soft. I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn't make the progress I needed."

His first stop was six laps before Leclerc's and when the Monegasque emerged back on to the track, Hamilton was right behind him and was initially faster.

At one stage, he pointed out to the team that he had "lost two seconds on that lap", but the team decided not to invert the cars. Hamilton followed Leclerc within two seconds for a further 10 laps before slowly starting to lose ground a couple of laps before the VSC.

Vasseur said the team decided to leave Leclerc in front because he had pitted later than Hamilton.

"The tyre advantage was for Charles, that he pitted six laps later," Vasseur said. "I think it was the right call."

However, that argument appears to be somewhat undermined by the fact that the medium tyre emerged as the worst option for the race - as Hamilton had found out in the first stint and other drivers found later on.

Leclerc was put back on the soft when he stopped under the VSC.

Hamilton's error means Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli is in a position to clinch his first world title at the next race, the US Grand Prix in Austin, after finishing third behind race winner Max Verstappen and Leclerc.

Antonelli's lead over team-mate George Russell, who finished ninth after starting from the back of the grid, has extended to 102 points and 111 over Hamilton.

The Italian needs to leave Austin with an advantage of at least 125 points to clinch the title, with five races at most remaining after that.

He will do so if he wins the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower at the Circuit of the Americas on 25 October.

If he becomes champion this year, the 20-year-old will be the youngest in Formula 1 history.

Asked if he would be daring to dream about the title on the flight home, he said: "For sure, but at the same time, I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can.

"The mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can.

"This weekend I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin.

"But at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that."

There is some doubt about the mathematics of the championship because it is not completely clear how many races are remaining.

F1 is pushing ahead with the original schedule, which ends with two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, despite the war in the Middle East, having been reassured the countries are safe.

But if the war intensifies before mid-November, those races will have to be cancelled. In that event, the season would end at Imola in Italy, on the same 6 December date as Abu Dhabi, after a two-week break following the Las Vegas race on 22 November.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said: "I haven't looked at it from that perspective, because the moment I have the thought of 'how many points is it actually, and when could he win it,' I remind myself that this is motor racing and crazy things have happened.

"The aim must be to score points, not to lose too many on the others, like today, gaining on Lewis, which was unexpected, and then it's going to come towards him, whether that's in Mexico or Brazil (the races immediately after Austin) or further down the line."

Mercedes 'need to go back to winning ways'

Mercedes split their cars between two different specifications in Singapore in an attempt to understand why a major upgrade introduced at the previous race in Malaysia did not work.

Antonelli drove the new spec and Russell the old, and by the end of the weekend the team said they had made some progress in understanding the new aerodynamic package.

Antonelli said: "We're just trying to understand how to extract more potential out of it because we do see the gains, we do see what it could bring.

"It's just that the window is very small at the moment where the car operates and is very sensitive to the way you drive it, the way you take a corner, the way you brake. So it reacts very differently.

"So hopefully now in Austin, we have three free practices, so we can be very open-minded with set-up and hopefully we can find a way and we can use the full potential of the package and finally see the gains."

Russell was asked how he viewed the rest of the season now the championship was almost over. He replied: "The goal is to improve the car. We were dominant for so long and since the break we have seen Red Bull be exceptionally fast on many different types of circuits and we need to go back to winning ways."

Verstappen may need 'new spine' after Austin bumps

Verstappen's victory was his first grand prix win in Singapore. It was also his second in succession, emphasising Red Bull's return to the front after a difficult start to the season.

Verstappen said: "Very different tracks that we have gone well at now. That's of course always nice to see.

"Our car has taken a really nice step forward. It's just been more driveable and more predictable. That's what I wanted and needed from the car to find that last step to fight up front. And I hope that we can carry that momentum forward.

"We don't really have anything to win in the championship, right? Kimi is miles ahead. I don't care if I'm second, third or fourth. It doesn't do anything. But I just want to have fun until the end, you know, try to go for a day's success."

But the four-time champion was cautious about the prospect of being competitive at every race before the end of the season.

"It's very difficult to say and I don't want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin," he said.

"Yeah, the last few weekends have been great. But I just take it race by race and once we are in Austin, then we'll see how it will go there. But it's again a very different track.

"From what I saw in WEC (the World Endurance Championship), the track is incredibly bumpy. Oh my God, yeah, I'll probably need to order a new spine, I think, after the weekend. Yeah, I'll become like Robocop. Yeah, crazy. That's again a new challenge for everyone, to deal with those bumps.

"And then we just go from there. We have to go to Mexico, high altitude, everything will run super hot, and we need to see how the engine is going to perform in that altitude, how the car is behaving, because it's very different.

"So there are so many different things that you can get right or wrong in those races."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver could clinch world championship at United States GP
articles.summary: He only has an outside chance, but Kimi Antonelli will have a first opportunity to make F1 history and become 2026's world champion as soon as the next race; watch the United States Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 on October 23-25
articles.body:
Mercedes' Antonelli increased his lead at the top of the Drivers' Championship to a season-high 102 points with a third-place finish in the Singapore Grand Prix.

George Russell remains second in the standings but a ninth-place finish after engine penalties had left him starting at the back of the grid dropped him beyond a century of points behind his team-mate for the first time, while Lewis Hamilton's late slide off the podium leaves the Ferrari driver 111 points off the pace in third place.

With such a large lead and with a scheduled six races left in the 2026 season, the world title now looks a formality for the 20-year-old Italian in just his second year of F1 to usurp Sebastian Vettel as the sport's youngest title winner.

A first chance - albeit an outside one - to clinch the crown will arrive as soon as the next race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas, live on Sky Sports F1 …

How Antonelli could win the title at the United States GP

There will be five scheduled races left - Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - after the United States Grand Prix takes place on Sunday October 25 and a maximum of 125 points left to play for.

To win the title in Austin, Antonelli needs to increase his championship lead by 23 points. For that to happen he must win the grand prix AND then hope both Russell and Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay within 124 points of him going to Mexico.

The permutations for Antonelli to become champion in Austin are:

Russell finishes ninth or lower (2 points or less)

Hamilton finishes fifth or lower (10 points or less)

Were Antonelli to win the race and Russell finish ninth, Antonelli would hold a 125-point lead over his team-mate with exactly 125 points left to play for. But that would still be enough for Antonelli to become champion, provided Hamilton was also still outside the top four in the race.

That is because victory in Austin would be the the Italian's ninth of the year and with Russell on three wins the Briton would only be able to get to a maximum of eight in the five races left. Antonelli would therefore be guaranteed the title on results countback, with race wins the first tiebreaker in event of an end-of-season points tie.

What about the other drivers still in mathematical contention?

Max Verstappen (119 points back), Charles Leclerc (125 points back) and Lando Norris (139 points back) all remain in mathematical title contention too after Singapore but would all be automatically knocked out by an Antonelli win in Austin wherever they finished that race.

'If I don't do my job well, then the result won't come' - Antonelli vows to stay focused

Antonelli is now within touching distance of an incredible historic achievement but stressed after Singapore that he cannot afford to let that fact distract him from his performance in Austin.

"I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can," he said.

"You know, the mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can. I think this weekend [in Singapore] I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that, you know, a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin.

"But, at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that."

Formula 1 next heads to The Americas for another triple header with the United States Grand Prix in Austin up first on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

articles.title: NASCAR Cup Playoffs Point Standings and Updated Schedule After 2026 Charlotte Results
articles.summary: Chase Briscoe fended off a last-lap surge from his teammate Christopher Bell to win the Bank of America 400 at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
articles.body:
Chase Briscoe fended off a last-lap surge from his teammate Christopher Bell to win the Bank of America 400 at Charlotte Motor Speedway.

The No. 19 car driver became the first racer to win consecutive races in the NASCAR postseason.

Briscoe's victory narrowed the gap between himself and NASCAR points leader Kyle Larson to 65 points.

Larson, Denny Hamlin, Bell and Briscoe left Charlotte as the top four drivers in the standings with four races left in the Chase.

Briscoe had a clear advantage at the front of the field for most of the closing stages of the race.

He took the lead on the race's final restart and appeared to be ready to cruise to victory.

However, Briscoe encountered lapped traffic on the final few laps, which allowed Bell to make a late push for the victory.

The pair of Joe Gibbs Racing teammates made contact with each other on the final lap and finished just a few car lengths apart.

Briscoe became the second driver to win multiple races in the NASCAR postseason. He also won last week at Las Vegas.

Larson, the current points leader, is the only other driver to win multiple races since the postseason began on September 6.

Larson still has a comfortable advantage over Hamlin, Bell and Briscoe in the points standings.

With four races left, Larson, Hamlin, Bell and Briscoe seem like the most likely options to capture the Chase title. There's 65 points between Larson in first and Briscoe in fourth. Ryan Blaney in fifth place is 85 points back of the points leader.

Next up for the Cup Series is a trip to Phoenix Raceway. Blaney was the race winner in Arizona back in March. Larson, Bell and Hamlin all finished in the top five in that race.

After Phoenix, the Cup Series finishes out at Talladega, Martinsville and Homestead-Miami.
